Update a block result that is on screen

Source: R/result-output.R
block_result_update.Rd

block_result_output() draws a result from scratch: the function it returns replaces the block's output, and the browser builds the result again. A table then loses its scroll position, its search text and its collapsed rows on every change of a control. A class that can change what it has drawn registers a method here. The method sends the new result to the browser itself, for example with session$sendCustomMessage() or with the update function of the widget it drew, and returns TRUE. The block then leaves its output as it is.

Usage

block_result_update(result, block, session, ...)

# Default S3 method
block_result_update(result, block, session, ...)

Arguments

result

The block's evaluated result.

block

The block object.

session

The block's Shiny module session.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

TRUE when the result on screen was updated. Anything else has the block draw the result from scratch.

When it is called

The block calls the method when the result it drew last is still on screen and the new result has the same class vector. In every other case it calls block_result_output():

  • the first result of a block, also of a block that was removed and added again under the same id;

  • a result of another class;

  • the first result after an error or after an input was unavailable;

  • a result whose predecessor has not reached the browser: a result evaluated twice while the block was hidden, or a second evaluation in the flush that drew the first;

  • after a method here returned anything but TRUE, or failed.

So a method can return FALSE for a change it cannot apply in place, such as a table with other columns, and the result is drawn from scratch.

A class without a method is drawn as before: the function its block_result_output() method returns is the block's output, unchanged.

What the method has to do

The output keeps the HTML the first render sent, and the render function of that render does not run again. So everything that follows the result has to be sent by this method: the data, and a caption the result draws itself. Use ids that are the same in every call, such as session$ns("table").

result_head() and result_titles() work as in block_result_output(). The head row starts empty before the call, so call result_head() with the same arguments as in the first render. result_titles(), called in the method, gives the sentence as it is now, and the block calls the method again when the sentence changes.

What the method can rely on

When the method is called, the HTML that block_result_output() drew for the last result was sent to the browser in an earlier flush. A message the method sends therefore arrives after that HTML, and after every message an earlier call sent.

It cannot rely on more than that. The block does not know whether the browser has the element in the page at this moment: a layout can take a hidden card out of the document. A message for an element that is not there is lost unless the widget keeps it, so a widget that can be hidden this way should apply the last message when it is attached again. If the browser attaches the output element again without a new evaluation, it draws the HTML of the first render.

The block also knows only the class of what it drew last, not which method drew it. A method that sometimes hands the result on with NextMethod() has to note that itself, and return FALSE here while the drawing in the page is not its own.

See also

block_result_output()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# A table widget with an update function of its own.
block_result_output.my_table <- function(result, block, session, ...) {
  id <- session$ns("table")
  shiny::renderUI(my_table_widget(result$data, id = id))
}

block_result_update.my_table <- function(result, block, session, ...) {
  update_my_table_widget(session, session$ns("table"), result$data)
  TRUE
}
} # }
